metric.ide_editor_support_quality.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-tooling--part-2--swift; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.breadth_maintenance: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--swift): Frozen 0-100 rubric, four equally-weighted dimensions applied identically to all languages: (1) first-party primary IDE completeness (autocomplete, refactoring, navigation, integrated build/run/debug/UI tooling); (2) multi-editor/cross-platform reach via LSP or equivalent; (3) breadth/currency of maintained alternative IDEs or editor plugins beyond the primary IDE; (4) reliability/maturity track record (issue reports, stability of indexing/completion). Each dimension scored 0-25 and summed.
component_findings.completion_types: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--swift): User reviews of Xcode note real reliability friction: 'Code completion and SwiftUI previews can be hit-or-miss' and indexing can be slow and get stuck on large projects, alongside forum reports of code completion, Quick Help, and Refactor breaking after indexer failures.

component_findings.refactor_actions: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--swift): Official cross-editor support exists through SourceKit-LSP, which Apple/the Swift project ships and which powers the official swiftlang/vscode-swift VS Code extension (code completion, code actions, diagnostics) rather than relying only on an unofficial community package.
